Subject: Renewal amendment: capacity commitment & burst flexibility

Hi Jurgen,

Thanks again for the time on Friday. Based on your usage trend during the POC and the traffic projections you shared, we've sketched a renewal amendment that adds a small reserved pool and an explicit burst/overflow path. High level:

- Core reserved: +8 RTX GPUs (reserved pool) for monthly commitment — 3.5x current committed throughput.
- Burst path: on-demand spillover to our shared capacity with an agreed soft cap and stepped pricing (see attached).
- Throughput SLO: 99th pct token latency target preserved for reserved capacity; burst best-effort but with priority tiers.

I've attached the amendment draft and throughput modeling. Would you and François be open to a quick call Tuesday to walk through pricing tiers and how burst billing would be calculated? If it looks good we can prepare a DocuSign amendment for signature.

Thanks,

Appreciate the summary. A couple quick notes from our side:

- The +8 GPUs for reserved capacity looks reasonable if throughput translates as modeled. We'll want a short ramp (1 month) to validate perf.

Jurgen —

Thanks, good questions. I pulled our legal and finance templates together and attached an updated amendment that includes two alternative burst controls:

Option A (Soft-cap, stepped billing)
- Burst available automatically up to 200% of reserved throughput.
- Billing: incremental per-token price in three tiers (0-25%, 25-75%, 75-200% of reserve).
- Notification: automated alerts at 60/80/95% of projected monthly spend.
- No automatic conversion to reserved; sustained usage >72 hours triggers manual account review and recommended scale-up.

Option B (Hard-cap with oversubscription waiver)
- Hard monthly monetary cap set by Neptune. Burst will be cut off when cap reached.
- Redwood can offer a short, manual uplift (temporary reserved top-up) if Neptune approves via a single-approver path.
- If long-term demand increases, we include an amendment path to convert burst to reserved with pro-rated pricing.

I've attached a "burst_pricing_cheatsheet.pdf" with cost examples for both options and a spreadsheet with modeled monthly spend. If you sign off on the preferred option I can drop a DocuSign amendment: https://www.docusign.com/sign/NEP-4821-amend

Proposed next steps for Tue 10/6 call:
- Walk through Option A vs B and numeric examples (10min)
- Confirm ramp and acceptance criteria during validation month (10min)
- Agree signature path and timing for go-live (10min)

--
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: burst_pricing_cheatsheet.pdf (PDF, 45KB), throughput_modeling.xlsx (updated)

Ben/Laura — internal note before Tue call. Highlights:

- Customer preference: leans toward a hard monetary cap (Option B). Finance wants a predictable max monthly spend.
- Risk: if we implement hard cap we need a fast manual uplift path (single-approver from Neptune) for when they legitimately exceed cap during product launches. Our ops team should be prepared to scope a temporary reserved top-up of +2-4 GPUs within 6 hours if approved.
- Suggest pricing for hard-cap: baseline reserved monthly + capped burst fee (flat monthly retainer for priority access) + per-token overage only if uplift path used. See my suggested numbers in the attached spreadsheet.

Can you review the uplift SLA (6 hours) and pricing split and flag any legal/ops concerns before the call? I'll push DocuSign if we land on Option B during the call.

Thanks,
Priyom

Priyom —

Thanks for the detailed options and the call earlier today. Neptune will proceed with Option B (hard monthly cap + manual uplift flow). A few final bullets before signature:

- We confirm the ramp: month 1 validation, then full reserved billing from month 2.
- Hard cap: set at $18,000/mo (includes reserved + capped burst fee).
- Manual uplift: single approver (Jurgen) can request temporary reserved top-up of up to +4 GPUs; Redwood commits to provisioning within 6 business hours when capacity is available. Any uplift beyond that will be subject to the uplift rate in the amendment.
- Please include a clause that if burst is cut off due to cap, Neptune may request a one-time emergency uplift that can be billed retroactively if approved.

If you add those items to the amendment I'll sign the DocuSign this afternoon.

Best,
Jurgen
